searchText: Hi all, <@360491619402776577> has been helping us on some hive updates to the "Invalid Ancestor" tests in this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/560 Basically all tests would now get the invalid payload retrieved from p2p via Sync, and ~~most of the clients are failing the tests again~~ some tests are failing again, but we think these are genuine new issues, so I wanted to share the results of running these changes before committing them. You can see the logs here: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/560#issuecomment-1184730752 Did <@425572898787426305> verify the changes as well? He was the one bringing up the attack vector, so I would like to make sure that the tests still cover that. In my opinion this implementation is more in line with the original idea of the attack scenario, the newPayload implementation was a workaround because we could not deliver invalid blocks via sync, but Marius wrote a node that now delivers them via p2p. Besu's hive run (https://hivetests2.ethdevops.io/viewer.html?file=results/besu/client-54563a8ecc04eda51f2643e40d0c496f41095b3029ac525e9b49ff8fdb83f0ab.log) failed with the following error: ``` java.lang.IllegalStateException: Attempt to start an already started BlockPropagationManager. ``` Running locally does not reproduce the issue. Has this been seen before ?

Hi all, <@360491619402776577> has been helping us on some hive updates to the "Invalid Ancestor" tests in this PR:
https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/560
Basically all tests would now get the invalid payload retrieved from p2p via Sync, and ~~most of the clients are failing the tests again~~ some tests are failing again, but we think these are genuine new issues, so I wanted to share the results of running these changes before committing them.
You can see the logs here: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/560#issuecomment-1184730752
